predecessors.name: Principality of Polotsk
predecessors.text: the Minsk lands that Gleb Vseslavich received when Polotsk was split into six principalities after Vseslav's death in 1101

successors.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
successors.text: the principality annexed de facto by Gediminas's Lithuania in 1326 (infobox and lead of the Minsk page); the body says it ceased to exist only after the Union of Horodło, 1413

ledger.x: 1101: Minsk becomes a principality under Gleb Vseslavich when Polotsk is divided.
1116: Vladimir Monomakh of Kiev besieges Minsk.
September 1119: Gleb dies a prisoner in Kiev and Minsk passes under Kievan influence.
1326: Minsk passes to the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.
1326: the Principality of Minsk ends, annexed de facto by the Grand Duchy of Lithuania (infobox 'Disestablished: 1326'); it becomes the Minsk Voivodeship after 1413.

wars.name: Monomakh's war against Gleb of Minsk
wars.outcome: Monomakh besieged Minsk for two months in 1116 and a peace was made; after Gleb's attack on Smolensk in 1117 Mstislav took Minsk and carried Gleb to Kiev, where he died in September 1119; Minsk fell under Kievan influence.

wars.name: Minsk and Drutsk against Polotsk (1164)
wars.outcome: With Lithuanian help Volodar of Minsk won a battle against the prince of Polotsk, which affirmed the principality's independence.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Rus' (Minsk escapes)
wars.outcome: Minsk escaped the invasion of 1237-1239; in 1249 a combined Minsk and Lithuanian army repelled a Tatar-Mongol invasion.

certainty.note: The pages give river basins and town lists, never a frontier line; the Drutsk and Vitebsk borders in particular are approximate.
